verdict.tagline: Cute auto battler offering tactical depth despite heavy random elements.
for_you_if: you enjoy casual tactical auto battlers
you like trying out weekly rotating pets
not_for_you_if: you dislike matches decided by random luck
you mind extra content locked behind purchases

distortion_flags.sentence: Review ratings rise after the initial refund window before dipping among long-term players.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Cute animal artwork masks heavy reliance on luck and locked content.

claims.claim: The game features cute animal artwork and simple, easy-to-understand combat mechanics.

citations.review_text: I like the cute little animals, and the combat is nice and easy to understand.

Super Auto Pets is already very fun and addictive. The cute animal designs and simple rules make it easy to learn, but building a powerful team requires real strategy. Even though I lost a few rounds, I always wanted to try just "one more game" with a new team combination. A great game for short play sessions. Definitely recommend!

claims.claim: Reviewers report that matches are heavily reliant on luck and random rolls rather than strategy, leading to situations where opponents have vastly superior stats.

citations.review_text: If you are new to this game, do not hope to win, unless the game decides it wants to let you win. Your gameplay will be VERY luck based on what the game decides you are allowed to get on your rolls.

The pets are cute, but it's far less strategy vs luck, and either you don't have enough gold to upgrade the pets (switching them out to better levels) or you don't get strong enough options for power-ups and replacer pets. The strategy element is minimal when, around turn 8 or so, it becomes impossible to defeat the opponent due to sheer difference in strength of what each team has available.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that additional packs and content require purchasing or a subscription rather than being unlockable through gameplay.

citations.review_text: suprisingly fun, could use more packs and creatures avaliable without buying stuff, dont mind having there be stuff you need to buy, but its more fun if most of it can be unlocked eventually or if there is still at least 3-5 sets of options for non bought things

The game is fun, but it sucks because you only have 2 options to actually enjoy more than 1% of the game:
1. Pay an absurd amount of money for all of the packs
2. Start a monthly subscription that you will probably forget you have and get overcharged

All of this can be immediately solved by just making the game cost money. The current business model is predatory and there is no good option. The overpriced pack that "includes all packs" does not include future packs, so they will siphon more money from you down the road, and the subscription is meant to make you a forced returning customer. There is no "pay money and own the game" option. I would highly advise against giving explicitly predatory companies any money.

Eh ... I'm not going to leave a negative review on a chill little free game, but to be honest, while the core concept is fun, it gets old pretty quickly unless you're willing to put in the $. There are no packs (== card sets) which can be unlocked through simply playing the game, besides the base set that you get at the start. However, since said base set only contains a few dozen pets, you will always run into the same pets and the same few viable builds, which at least for me made the game feel quite repetitive after less than 3 hours.

I personally would have preferred paying a purchase price for the game, then having access to all the unlocks through gameplay afterwards.

So, is the game bad ? No, it's fine. And above all, it's free, so you can just give it a shot and see for yourself. I for one feel like it's too limited and will therefore skip on the paid DLCs.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that keywords and game mechanics are not explained properly.

citations.review_text: This was hard to pick up at first, but when you get going you get into the groove! The Mechanics are easy and its a fun game with a bit of luck added but thats what makes it special. It does get repetitive if you do not play for the add ons but thats it.

Game mechanics don't even work properly half the time. Keywords are not explained, and don't do what you think they would do half the time. Units have as much counter synergy as they do synergy. It's a half finished game, with over $100 of micro transactions inside. It's "free to play" for the wattered down, partial access version, then $10-40, just for packs.... let alone everything else. So you can play the demo for free, or they want $40-100+ for the cheap ass, bargain bin auto battler. There is 50 other versions of this game but better out there. 

EDIT: I had to add this, but why is there 100s of positive reviews for this game on here with 0.1-0.3 hours played, what's going on steam?!...

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the matchmaking system as prone to pairing players against heavily targeted, high-level counter-compositions, particularly in modes like the turtle pack.

citations.review_text:
好玩的游戏模式、多样化流派设计👍

But the game experience is extremely terrible, with updates and changes that don't consider players' needs. 😡
The game has many issues that degrade player experience, particularly the matchmaking system, which often pairs players with highly targeted opponents leading to losses. This effect becomes more pronounced in packs with larger player numbers, such as the turtle pack, where only "old oil sticks" (scheming and cunning players) are matched. Additionally, game updates frequently deviate in odd directions.
After playing for a few years, I'm more and more disappointed with this game each time. Enough is enough

 I'd say 90% of this games content is locked behind a pay wall. A large pay wall. I actually bought one of the packs because even though I hate pay to win games, I really liked this one's aesthetics and mechanics however even after paying it was still mostly luck of the draw whether or not I had any chance of winning, because I only bought 1. That's not to say it is impossible to win. Even before buying a pack I would win every handful of games...until they nerfed multiple of the free pets. claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features asynchronous gameplay and lack of time limits, allowing matches to be paused, played on mobile devices, or left open during breaks without penalties.

citations.review_text: I have wayyy too many hours in this game not to leave a review, +the mobile version hours which arent logged. This game is a fantastic blend of deck building, gambling, and asynchronous gameplay which means no waiting time. Honestly, I had to uninstall this game for a while because it was so addicting.

I absolutely love this game (if you cannot tell by my hours played, which does NOT include the countless hours I've spent on my mobile version) as a person who loves strategy, collecting, auto-battlers, and considering what to do next in any given game that I'm playing. I love the fact that you can set up a comp/composition in the game and focus on a specific style of play or just go wild if you're trying to collect achievements. I also like that you can either choose to play a randomized pack each week, focus on specific "sets" of pets so it's always pets in that collection from opponents and yourself, or you can choose to make your own collection of pets and do a "wild" mode - which I have used to complete achievements for various pets. 

With each pet having it's own ability and pets synergizing with one another, you can have endless set-ups to have unique experiences each run you play - and through my many hours of playing I've found you can match pets up together that you wouldn't think would pair well together to get fun game play or to hunt achievements. 

I like that each time you play you can pick it up and get a few matches in or even just run your rounds till you win or lose the 10 rounds and start a new run on a quick break or while waiting for an event or appointment. I often pick it up on my mobile version at work on my breaks and have a blast each time playing my matches. It's easy and fun to pick up and I feel like does not take much time to get rolling with the various game modes/archetypes it offers.

It does offer paid versions of "packs" to unlock more pets, but I feel like for the price you pay and the endless hours of fun it can offer, it's totally worth it paying the price for the extra packs. And if you're ever uncertain, you can always try the weekly packs which sometimes offer a random mish-mash of pets to try out!

The game is a lovely combination of cute and challenging. Having weekly packs presents a new "meta" to solve or subvert every week, which feels akin to playing connections or wordle. The games are relatively short, and with no time limits you can take endless breaks without penalty, making it an easy game to pick up and put down, or have open on another tab. But it also has a lot of room for experimentation, with some pretty ridiculous builds if you plan your team correctly.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game offers a free-to-play experience centered around the base turtle pack, while additional packs containing extra pets and content are available for purchase.

citations.review_text:
TLDR: It is cute, fairly fun, free to "play" and very pay to win. ¿stole my money?

 I'd say 90% of this games content is locked behind a pay wall. A large pay wall. I actually bought one of the packs because even though I hate pay to win games, I really liked this one's aesthetics and mechanics however even after paying it was still mostly luck of the draw whether or not I had any chance of winning, because I only bought 1. That's not to say it is impossible to win. Even before buying a pack I would win every handful of games...until they nerfed multiple of the free pets. It felt like every time a winning strategy would come up that used the free pets, one or more of the pets involved would get "tweaked". They've improved the match making a little, still sucks. I get it, they need to make money and if I had paid over $100 on what is essentially booter packs I'd expect to dominate the competition. I wish they just had a free demo and then a full game that was like $10-15 or something. I really do like this game and would have kept playing it despite its shortcomings but for some reason when I launched the game today I was logged out and it said none of my emails are registered to an account. I'm not too mad, could've been an accident, may be my fault somehow (can't think of how but still) and it finally got me to drop this game and write a review.

This game is adorable, interactive, and has plenty of options for casual and competitive play for those interested in a more serious game mode once they've learned the ropes join the DOJO, a discord server where there are weekly, monthly and yearly tournaments held with actual prizes by the community. Also TWG updates the game regularly, takes player opinion into account when making changes and continues to roll out new pets, toys and packs for us to work with. Excellent game, 11/10. Does require time if you want to be competitive but also a great game to just chill and play on your phone, tablet or computer. The best part, it's 100% free to play (unless you want to buy additional packs to play after mastering turtle pack, or for in-game cosmetics that have 0 effect on gameplay quality or interactions, but I still grabbed all of them to support one of my absolute favorite games. Check it out, it's free, it's fun, and a typical game takes all of 5-10 minutes once you understand how it works and the pets involved.
